CA.notes: These are the federal 'general holidays' (federally regulated employers). Provinces set their own lists, and Thanksgiving is not statutory in every province. Good Friday is a general holiday; Easter Monday is not.

MX.notes: Día de Muertos is not a mandatory rest day under art. 74.

BR.notes: Carnival is only a 'ponto facultativo' (Portaria MGI 11.460/2025). Finados (2 Nov, All Souls) is national but was not mapped to dia-de-muertos.

AR.notes: Carnival Monday and Tuesday are 'feriados nacionales inamovibles'. Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are non-working days only for Muslims (art. 3), so they are excluded.

GB.notes: Only days common to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. Easter Monday is not a Scottish bank holiday; St Patrick's Day is Northern Ireland only.

FR.notes: Easter counts via Lundi de Pâques. Only 1 May is a mandatory day off by law; the other fêtes légales are days off by agreement or custom.

DE.notes: BMI lists nine holidays protected in all Länder (incl. Ostermontag, 1. and 2. Weihnachtstag). The page returned HTTP 400 to direct fetches; its text was read through the search index.

ES.notes: Lunes de Pascua is regional only; Eid holidays apply only in Ceuta and Melilla.

IT.notes: Easter counts via Lunedì dopo Pasqua.

NL.notes: Official holidays, but whether employees get the day off depends on their CAO.

PL.authority: Zielona Linia (Polish public employment services, Ustawa o dniach wolnych od pracy)

GR.authority: Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Greek missions in the USA)
GR.notes: Greek holidays (G) on the mission list include Orthodox Good Friday and Easter Monday (13 Apr 2026). mfa.gr returns 403 to direct fetches; its text was read through the search index.

RU.authority: Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (Labour Code art. 112)
RU.notes: Orthodox Easter is not a federal non-working day.

ET.authority: U.S. Embassy Addis Ababa holiday calendar (Ethiopian holidays marked ET)
ET.notes: Embassy page used because no Ethiopian government list was reachable.

NG.authority: U.S. Mission Nigeria holiday calendar (Nigerian holidays marked NG)
NG.notes: The Ministry of Interior's holiday notices (interior.gov.ng) were unavailable (404/503). Easter counts via Easter Monday.

KE.notes: Idd-ul-Azha (Part II) is a public holiday only for Muslims, and Diwali (Part III) only for Hindus, so both are excluded.

ZA.authority: South African Government (Public Holidays Act 36 of 1994)
ZA.notes: Easter counts via Family Day, the Monday after Easter Sunday.

EG.authority: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
EG.notes: Coptic Christmas (7 Jan) is mapped to christmas-julian. Sham El-Nessim (Monday after Coptic Easter) was not mapped to orthodox-pascha. presidency.eg returns 403 to direct fetches; its text was read through the search index.

SA.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

AE.authority: UAE Government portal (Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024)

TR.authority: Law 2429 on National Holidays and General Holidays (mevzuat.gov.tr)

IR.authority: Embassy of Belgium in Tehran (2026 holiday list)
IR.notes: Partial: Iranian government lists were unreachable (mfa.gov.ir redirect loop, calendar.ut.ac.ir 404). Secondary sources say Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are also official Iranian holidays, but no government page confirming them was read, so they are left out.

IN.authority: Government of India, DoPT Office Memorandum (holidays for central government offices)
IN.notes: These are among the 14 holidays compulsory for all central government offices nationwide; states and private employers set their own lists. Holi and Vaisakhi are optional/restricted, so excluded. The source is a mirror of the official O.M.

PK.notes: 25 December is listed as 'Quaid-e-Azam Day/ Christmas'. New Year's Day, Holi, Easter, Diwali and Guru Nanak's birthday are optional holidays only, so excluded.

BD.authority: Embassy of Bangladesh, Tokyo (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
BD.notes: The mission list also includes Japanese holidays, which are ignored here. Vesak is Budha Purnima.

LK.authority: Deputy High Commission of Sri Lanka, Chennai
LK.notes: The mission list mixes Sri Lankan and Indian holidays. The Sri Lankan government gazette was not reachable. Sinhala and Tamil New Year is not mapped to songkran.

NP.authority: Nepal Rajpatra (Ministry of Home Affairs notice for 2083 BS)
NP.notes: From section 2.1 (festivals that are public holidays nationwide). Holi (Fagu Purnima) is on different days: Chait 7 in the 56 hill and mountain districts and Chait 8 in the Terai districts. Diwali is Tihar (from Laxmi Puja). Guru Nanak Jayanti is a holiday only for Nepali Sikhs, so excluded.

CN.authority: General Office of the State Council

HK.authority: Hong Kong SAR Government (gazetted general holidays)
HK.notes: Easter counts via Easter Monday. Mid-Autumn counts via 'The day following the Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival'. The Birthday of the Buddha (8th day, 4th lunar month) was not mapped to vesak.

TW.authority: Directorate-General of Personnel Administration, Executive Yuan
TW.notes: 1 January is officially 'Founding Day of the Republic of China'. 25 December is Constitution Day, not Christmas. The Lantern Festival is not a day off.

KR.authority: Regulations on Public Holidays of Government Offices (KLRI translation)
KR.notes: Buddha's Birthday (8th day, 4th lunar month) is a public holiday but was not mapped to vesak.

VN.notes: Tết Trung Thu is not a public holiday.

TH.notes: This is the nationwide financial-institution holiday list, which mirrors the Cabinet's government holidays for these days. The Cabinet Secretariat's own list was not reached. Vesak is Visakha Bucha. Chinese New Year is a holiday only in some southern provinces.

MY.authority: Embassy of Malaysia, Tokyo (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
MY.notes: The Prime Minister's Department table (kabinet.gov.my/storage/2025/08/HKA-2026.pdf) was unreachable. New Year's Day and Deepavali appear on the mission list but are not observed in every state (New Year: not in Johor, Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis and Terengganu; Deepavali: not in Sarawak, per the federal table as reported), so they are excluded as not nationwide.

ID.authority: Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Culture (SKB 3 Menteri 2026)
ID.notes: Easter counts via Easter Sunday (Hari Kebangkitan Yesus Kristus). Vesak is Waisak.

PH.authority: Philippine Embassy Madrid list, citing Proclamation No. 1006 (2025)
PH.notes: pco.gov.ph and officialgazette.gov.ph block automated fetches. New Year's Day and Christmas come from RA 9849's list of regular holidays (read on lawphil.net, a non-government mirror). Chinese New Year is a special non-working day.

AU.notes: New Year's Day, Easter Monday and Christmas Day appear in every state and territory list. Australia Day (26 January) is a public holiday in every state and territory.

unsourced.UA: Labour Code art. 73 lists holidays, but under martial law (Law 2136-IX, art. 6) they are not days off, according to State Labour Service reporting. The official text on zakon.rada.gov.ua could not be fetched (403 / JS render).
